correctness.rationale: Write T=uv* with ||v||=1. The defining quadratic operator equation reduces exactly to L(2−s)=1 and ||b||²=(s−1)²/(2−s). The canonical inverse is S=vw* with w=2u−La v and w*u=1; hence ST=vv* and TS=uw* are idempotents. For any common positive metric G, GP=PG enforces Gv=gv and GQ=Q*G enforces Gu=cw for c>0. Orthogonal components give g=c(2−L) for a≠0 and Gb=2cb. Thus positivity is equivalent to L<2, realized by G0=(2−L)P+2(I−P). When a,b≠0, forced orthogonal eigenvalues prove the exact condition-number minimum 2/(2−L), attained by G0; at s=0,1 ordinary MP inversion already holds. The endpoint 2×2 witness has QP=0 but PQ≠0, forbidding simultaneous self-adjointness. The supplementary executable checks sampled identities but does not replace these proofs.

value.rationale: The source explicitly asks whether the canonical inverse can be made Moore–Penrose by changing the inner product. The rank-one classification resolves this open-ended qualitative question negatively at a natural exact boundary, positively below it, and sharpens the positive region by the optimal Hilbert metric distortion and its divergence. The result is dimension-independent, not simply the routine observation that the standard inverse is not Moore–Penrose.
